transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt, and I kept having these awful thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. Like if I put one photo in the wrong place or chose the wrong color, it would mean I didn’t love her enough. They didn’t feel like normal creative doubts—I couldn’t just brush them off.

When you have these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like rechecking the photos, redoing the arrangement, or seeking reassurance—to make the bad feeling go away?

Yes. I reread the label text and keep nudging the same objects around on the table. I’ll check photos of the layout over and over until it feels settled. Part of me knows it already looks fine, but I keep doing it anyway, and it eats up a lot of studio time.
About how many hours a day would you say these checking and rearranging behaviors, along with the distressing thoughts, take up?

It’s not all day—I’m still getting most of my work done—but it adds up. I’ve already lost enough studio time that I missed a grant deadline, and I backed out of a gallery talk I actually wanted to do.

Do you notice similar intrusive thoughts and the urge to check or repeat things in other parts of your life—like at home, with relationships, or other work projects—or has this been limited to this particular memorial piece?

It’s really been centered on the memorial piece. I keep getting stuck on this fear that a wrong choice—where a photo goes, even a color—would somehow mean I didn’t love my aunt enough or that I was disrespecting her. They feel awful and unwanted, not like regular indecision about the work.
How long ago did your aunt pass away, and how long have you been experiencing these intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors since then?
I’m not sure I can give you an exact timeline. It’s been since I started working on the piece, but I don’t really know when the thoughts and checking crossed into this being a problem.
Roughly how many weeks or months have you been working on this memorial piece and experiencing these thoughts and checking behaviors?
I honestly can’t pin it down to a number of weeks or months. I’ve been working on it for a while, but I don’t know exactly when the checking and the thoughts started taking over.

When you're in the middle of these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt, do you recognize at that moment that the fear is excessive or doesn't quite make logical sense, even though it still feels urgent?

Part of me knew it didn’t really make sense that a color or photo placement could prove I didn’t love her. But it still felt so urgent and awful that I couldn’t just let it go like a normal creative decision.
Aside from these intrusive thoughts about the artwork, do you find yourself missing your aunt intensely, longing to see her, or spending a lot of time thinking about her and the loss itself?
I’m not really sure. I do think about her sometimes, but I haven’t noticed spending a lot of time just longing for her or focused on the loss itself.
